SMTO-LLM-0083 — An older SMTO version held back a model request

GUID: 16bcd7e3-6174-5fdf-b759-81048a35e0b3
Slug: inference-admission-unconfirmed
Domain: LLM · Subsystem: inference_admission

What happened

  • This message comes from an older SMTO version that could hold back model requests after an unclear connection result. That system has been removed, and the records of what the Run did are unchanged.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the conversation for that Run and read its activity to see which steps finished. The old Run may have completed some actions, and repeating them could do the same work twice.
  2. Send a follow-up asking the Agent to continue only the unfinished parts. Current SMTO no longer holds requests back this way, so continuing proceeds normally.
  3. If a brand-new request shows this message, ask the person who manages SMTO to restart the server so it runs the updated version. New work can only show this message when the server is still running old code.

What success looks like

  • New requests get model replies without this message, and the old Run's finished steps are not repeated.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Don't rerun the whole old Task from the beginning; steps that already finished could happen twice.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • Historical identity: a retired inference-pool admission gate blocked a model request after uncertain transport completion; current controllers issue no endpoint tickets and have no such gate.

What this means

  • This retained error describes an earlier admission system that could block replacement calls after uncertain transport completion. Current controllers have no endpoint tickets or reconciliation gate. Historical operation receipts and outcomes are unchanged.

Why this can happen

  • An earlier controller used the now-retired inference admission gate.

How to diagnose it

  • Compare the recorded occurrence time and controller version with the current process.

How to fix it

  • Resolvable only from the catalog (get_error_details in src/error_catalog/registry.py). Inspect the historical run's operation receipts before resuming its preserved work; if newly submitted work raises SMTO-LLM-0083, the Server is still running a build from before the gate was removed and must be restarted on current code.
  • Inspect the historical run and its operation receipts before resuming preserved work. Current controllers need no inference ticket reconciliation. If newly submitted work still produces this error, verify that the controller is running the updated version.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect the historical run and its operation receipts before resuming preserved work. Current controllers need no inference ticket reconciliation. If newly submitted work still produces this error, verify that the controller is running the updated version.

How to verify the fix

  • The updated controller sends new model requests without endpoint tickets. Existing operations retain their receipts.

What not to do

  • Do not treat socket cancellation or URL separation as proof of backend completion or cache isolation.

Technical notes

  • Historical records remain readable; this identity is no longer emitted by model requests.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
